subject: community-medicine
title: Barrier Methods, Vasectomy, and Tubectomy: Permanent Contraception

steps.title: Male condom: dual protection
steps.tx: The **male condom (Nirodh)** is a latex sheath that collects semen and blocks sperm, giving a typical use Pearl index near thirteen per hundred woman years and near two with perfect use. It alone among contraceptives also protects against human immunodeficiency virus and other sexually transmitted infections, which is why programmes call it the dual protection method and distribute it free through health facilities and social marketing.
steps.say: Condoms prevent pregnancy and infections together. Perfect use fails about two per hundred yearly; typical use fails about thirteen.

nodes.label: Withdraw held at base, single use only

steps.title: Female condom and diaphragm
steps.tx: The **female condom** is a polyurethane pouch with rings at both ends that lines the vagina, controlled by the woman, reusable in no circumstance, and protective against infections like its male counterpart. The diaphragm is a latex dome fitted over the cervix with spermicide, sized by examination, left in for six hours after intercourse, and rarely used in India because fitting and follow up are provider dependent.
steps.say: The female condom gives women barrier control with infection protection. Diaphragms need fitting and spermicide, so India barely uses them.

steps.title: Spermicides and their limits
steps.tx: Chemical **spermicides in contraception** (nonoxynol nine foams, gels, and the Indian Today sponge of polyurethane impregnated with spermicide) kill sperm on contact but fail in fifteen to thirty per hundred woman years alone, and frequent nonoxynol use can irritate mucosa and paradoxically raise HIV acquisition risk. Their rational role is as diaphragm partners or backup, never as a programme mainstay.
steps.say: Spermicides alone fail too often to recommend solo. The sponge and foams belong as backups, not primary family planning.

steps.title: No scalpel vasectomy
steps.tx: **No scalpel vasectomy** reaches the vas deferens through a tiny puncture with special forceps, occluding both ends by ligation, excision of a segment, cautery, or fascial interposition, in a ten minute outpatient procedure under local anaesthesia. It does not affect erection, ejaculation volume noticeably, testosterone, or libido. Sterility is confirmed only after semen examination shows azoospermia, typically after twenty ejaculations or three months.
steps.say: No scalpel vasectomy takes ten minutes through a puncture. It changes neither potency nor hormones, but needs a semen check before reliance.

steps.tx: **No scalpel vasectomy** delivers each vas deferens through a tiny puncture using special forceps, then occludes both sides by ligation, excision of a segment, cautery, or fascial interposition. The outpatient procedure takes about ten minutes under local anaesthesia. Erection, testosterone, libido, and noticeable ejaculate volume are preserved. Sterility is not assumed until semen shows azoospermia, usually after about twenty ejaculations or three months, so another method is required until that check.
steps.say: Special forceps bring the vas out through a puncture for a ten minute operation under local anaesthetic. Potency and hormones stay the same, but semen must show no sperm after about twenty ejaculations or three months before the method is trusted.

vis.alt: Ring forceps and dissecting forceps used for no scalpel vasectomy lie together as the instrument set.
vis.caption: The ring clamp and pointed dissecting forceps are the only special tools needed to deliver the vas through a puncture. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Tubectomy and minilaparotomy
steps.tx: Female sterilisation occludes both fallopian tubes, most often by **minilaparotomy tubectomy** through a small suprapubic incision in the postpartum or interval period. Failure runs near five per thousand procedures, and when pregnancy occurs after tubectomy the ectopic share is high, so any missed period after sterilisation needs urgent evaluation. Reversal succeeds best after clip or ring occlusion with long remaining tube length.
steps.say: Tubectomy blocks both tubes through a small incision. Failure is rare, but a later pregnancy is often ectopic and dangerous.

steps.title: Vasectomy versus tubectomy for the couple
steps.tx: For a couple sure their family is complete, **vasectomy versus tubectomy comparison** favours vasectomy on safety, cost, failure rate, and recovery, yet tubectomy dominates Indian statistics because of camp organisation, incentives history, and male myths. Counselling must state permanence honestly: both are intended irreversible, reversal is uncertain microsurgery, and regret concentrates in young, low parity, or pressured acceptors.
steps.say: Vasectomy is safer, cheaper, and surer than tubectomy, yet India does far more tubectomies. Both must be counselled as permanent.

steps.title: Sterilisation eligibility and consent
steps.tx: Indian standards for **sterilisation eligibility and consent** require a married client aged twenty two to forty nine years with at least one child above one year, free informed consent of the client (spousal consent is not legally mandatory though joint counselling is encouraged), sound mind, and no past sterilisation. Medical officers certify fitness, and compensation covers wage loss through programme insurance that also indemnifies failure and complications.
steps.say: Sterilisation needs age twenty two to forty nine, a living child, and the client's own free consent. Programme insurance covers failure and complications.

nodes.label: Procedure with insurance and follow up

steps.title: Complications and failure handling
steps.tx: Sterilisation **complications and failure management** spans anaesthetic events, bowel or vessel injury in tubectomy, haematoma and chronic pain after vasectomy, and method failure presenting as pregnancy. The family planning indemnity scheme pays defined compensation for failure, complication treatment, and death, provided claims are filed within the stipulated period with procedure records, converting rare mishaps into a trust preserving system.
steps.say: Rare failures and injuries are covered by the indemnity scheme. Document the procedure well so genuine claims succeed quickly.

steps.title: Couple years of protection
steps.tx: Programmes compare methods by **couple years of protection**, the estimated protected years from one unit: roughly fifteen years credited per sterilisation, ten per Copper T 380A in extended conventions, one hundred twenty condoms per couple year, and fifteen pill cycles per couple year. The metric lets stores convert commodities into equivalent protection and exposes why long acting methods dominate cost effectiveness tables.
steps.say: Couple years of protection converts commodities into protected time. One sterilisation credits about fifteen years, which is why it tops value tables.
